[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The network-tier resource is configured for this project but does not wait for the Compute API activation resource. When Compute API is included in the module's services, Terraform could attempt this operation before that API is enabled.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Compute default network tier resource calls the Compute API, but it has no ordering dependency on project service activation. If compute.googleapis.com is enabled by this module, activation should complete before this operation.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier calls the Compute API (projects.setDefaultNetworkTier) and must run after the Compute API is enabled. Its sibling in main.tf, google_compute_project_metadata_item.default, carries depends_on = [google_project_service.project_services], but default_network_tier has no such ordering (its only reference is var.default_network_tier, and the project comes via local.project.project_id). Add google_project_service.project_services to depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier configures a Compute Engine project setting, which requires compute.googleapis.com to be enabled. Unlike google_compute_project_metadata_item.default, it has no depends_on on google_project_service.project_services, so it can be applied before the Compute API finishes enabling.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier configures the Compute Engine default network tier, so the Compute API must be enabled first. It has no dependency on google_project_service.project_services (unlike the sibling google_compute_project_metadata_item.default).

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier sets the project default network tier via the Compute Engine API, which must be enabled in the project before this call succeeds. The adjacent google_compute_project_metadata_item.default resource in the same file explicitly depends on google_project_service.project_services for exactly this reason; the network tier resource lacks the same ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier sets the project-wide Compute Engine default network tier via the Compute API, but has no dependency on google_project_service.project_services. The sibling resource google_compute_project_metadata_item.default depends on the service activation for the same compute.googleapis.com API; this resource should too, otherwise creation can race API enablement on a new project.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
google_compute_project_default_network_tier.default_network_tier calls the Compute Engine project setDefaultNetworkTier API, which requires compute.googleapis.com to be enabled. It is only gated on var.default_network_tier being set — unlike google_compute_project_metadata_item.default (which both guards on compute being in available_services and depends on the service resource), it has no ordering with respect to API activation and can fail on a fresh project. Add a depends_on for google_project_service.project_services.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Shared VPC service-project association performs a Compute operation on this project but only waits for the VPC Service Controls resources. It should also wait for project service activation so the Compute API is enabled before the association is created.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Attaching this project as a Shared VPC service project requires the Compute API, but the resource does not wait for this module's project service activation to complete.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service associates this project as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute API to be enabled in the project first. Unlike its siblings google_compute_shared_vpc_host_project.shared_vpc_host (which depends_on google_project_service.project_services) and service_projects (which inherits that ordering), this resource only depends on the VPC-SC perimeter resources and has no path to google_project_service.project_services. Add it to depends_on (no clean data reference exists since the project id is referenced via local.project.project_id).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_compute_shared_vpc_service_project.shared_vpc_service attaches this project as a Shared VPC service project, which requires the Compute API in the service project. It only depends on the VPC-SC perimeter resources, not on google_project_service.project_services.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
Log-based metrics require the Cloud Logging API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation. It can race logging.googleapis.com enablement when that service is managed here.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Logs-based metric creation uses the Cloud Logging API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation to finish.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
Project log exclusions require the Cloud Logging API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation and can race logging.googleapis.com enablement.

----------------------------------------

Project logging exclusion creation uses the Cloud Logging API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation to finish.

Log scopes use the Cloud Logging API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation and can race logging.googleapis.com enablement.

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Log-scope creation uses the Cloud Logging API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation to finish.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
Monitoring notification channels require the Cloud Monitoring API, but these resources do not wait for project service activation and can race monitoring.googleapis.com enablement.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Notification-channel creation uses the Cloud Monitoring API, but this resource does not wait for project service activation to finish.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels creates Monitoring notification channels in this project, but has no dependency on the project's API enablement. If monitoring.googleapis.com is among the enabled services, the channel creation can race with (or precede) API activation and fail. Sibling observability/operational resources in this module (sinks, IAM bindings, quotas, compute metadata) all declare depends_on on google_project_service.project_services; this resource should too.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_monitoring_notification_channel.channels is created against the Cloud Monitoring API but has no dependency on google_project_service.project_services. When the project is newly created by this module, the monitoring.googleapis.com API activation runs asynchronously after project creation; without ordering, channel creation can race API enablement and fail (the sibling google_logging_project_sink.sink already carries exactly this depends_on).

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
Monitoring alert policies require the Cloud Monitoring API, but these resources do not otherwise wait for project service activation. An implicit reference to a managed notification channel, when present, does not itself order the channel after API activation.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
Alert-policy creation uses the Cloud Monitoring API, but it does not wait for project service activation to finish; a dependency on a notification channel, when present, does not ensure the API is enabled.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts creates Cloud Monitoring alert policies in this project, which requires the Monitoring API to be enabled first. It references notification channels via an attribute but has no ordering against API activation. All other API-dependent resources in this module gate on google_project_service.project_services via depends_on; this resource should as well.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_monitoring_alert_policy.alerts is created against the Cloud Monitoring API but only depends on the notification channels (which are themselves unordered with respect to API activation). It needs a dependency on google_project_service.project_services so monitoring.googleapis.com is fully enabled before the alert policy is written, matching the ordering google_logging_project_sink.sink already has.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary attaches metric scopes via the Monitoring API, which must be enabled in the project before the resource can be created. There is no attribute reference or depends_on ordering it after google_project_service.project_services, unlike every other API-dependent resource in this module.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
google_monitoring_monitored_project.primary attaches this project as a monitored project in a metrics scope via the Cloud Monitoring API, but has no dependency on google_project_service.project_services. On a freshly created project the monitoring API may still be activating when this resource is created, causing a spurious failure.
